messages.subject: sequenza output to gistic input
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to use sequenza output for gistic2 analysis ftp://ftp.broadinstitute.org/pub/GISTIC2.0/GISTICDocumentation_standalone.htm

but how to generate the input for gistic2 from sequenza?
The input files for gistic2:

Segmentation File (-seg)                                      REQUIRED

The segmentation file contains the segmented data for all the samples identified by GLAD, CBS, or some other segmentation algorithm.  (See GLAD file format in the Genepattern file formats documentation.)  It is a six column, tab-delimited file with an optional first line identifying the columns.  Positions are in base pair units.

  The column headers are:

(1)  Sample           (sample name)

(2)  Chromosome  (chromosome number)

(3)  Start Position  (segment start position, in bases)

(4)  End Position   (segment end position, in bases)

(5)  Num markers      (number of markers in segment)

(6)  Seg.CN       (log2() -1 of copy number)

Example Segmentation File

Markers File (-mk)                                                  OPTIONAL

The markers file identifies the marker positions used in the original dataset (before segmentation) for array or capture experiments. As of GISTIC release 2.0.23, the markers file is an optional input - if omitted, pseudo markers are generated as uniformly as possible using the maxspace input parameter.

The markers file is a three column, tab-delimited file with an optional header.  The column headers are:

(1)  Marker Name

(2)  Chromosome

(3)  Marker Position        (in bases)

I've read https://www.biostars.org/p/158408/
and https://groups.google.com/a/broadinstitute.org/forum/#!searchin/gistic-forum/whole$20exome/gistic-forum/BUjH7LF3T70/5rWlcPI5DAAJ

I do not know how to get the number of markers and the marker file from sequenza.

Thanks!
Tommy

messages.subject: sequenza on hg38?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

Does sequenza support hg38? The error message "Error : assembly must be one of hg19, hg18, hg17 or hg16" seems to indicate that it doesn't.

cheers,
/Christoffer

messages.subject: Re: sequenza on hg38?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christoffer,

sequenza per-se doesn’t really deal with genome build, the problem is in the copynumber package used for the segmentation.

here you can find how to use a modified version of copynumber to enable hg38, or any other genome build:

https://github.com/aroneklund/copynumber

Cheers

Francesco

messages.subject: Re: sequenza-utils pileup2seqz time cosuming
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Francesco

I also recognize that all het normal loci match none AB.tumor allele in seqz file. Here, you said the infomation is discarded. It means we should accept an assumption that any site in tumor doesn't mutate to a third even forth allele, meanwhile the mutation.txt result file can just contain the other allele's copy number reletive to the A allele in normal, but I think this assumption is not so acceptable in cancer genomics. I wonder know the reason to discard tumor allele info at normal het loci. Is it difficult to estimate the parameters using these sites infomaton?

Another affect is, I guess, the lack of info here will lead the subclone estimation producing some bias. If the individual's heterozygosity is high, a lot sites will lost some infomation. Because some polymorphism sites may located in mutation hotspot, and in cancer evolution, these sites may generate new mutation more easily than other sites. Maybe these sites can provide the detail of cancer subclone evolution.

I want to reconstruct the consensus sequence of each tumor sample. If some loci contain more than allele, I will use degenerate bases symbol according IUPAC. Can you give me some suggestion to do that?

My best,
Xuan

On Monday, March 27, 2017 at 7:37:23 PM UTC+8, Francesco Favero wrote:
> Hi Yang,
>
> In the seqz file you can have the information in the AB.tumor column, if the locus is homozygous.
> You will have the frequency of the alternative nucleotide in a format such as A0.1:C0.34, that indicates the frequencies of the nucleotides other then the germline alele: in the specifc example 10% of nucleotides are As and 34% are Cs.
> If you sum all the frequency of the AB.tumor and the frequency in the A column (which is the frequency of the nucleotide in the  AB.normal column), you should have 1.
>
> if the position is heterozygous you have the frequency of the two alleles in the columns A and B. They should sum to 1, unless there is some reads which is not one of the 2 nucleotides (mutation/error information on het locus, is basically discarded)
>
> If you want a more genotype agnostic approach you could use the tool pileup2acgt. this converts a mpileup line into ACGT.
> You can tabix your pileup, query for the coordinate(s) with tabix and pipe the results to the acgt.
> I think now there are also native samtools options that allows to convert a bam to the number of ACGT, but you have the option also with sequenza-utils :).
>
> Best
>
> Francesco
>
> > On 24 Mar 2017, at 08.13, 11033...@qq.com wrote:
> >
> > I have another question.
> > I have a list of locus(e.g chr1 1435684), now I want to know the frequency of each allele (e.g A 0.3 G 0.7) at that location in my tumor sample. I wonder if I can get such information in the seqz data. Would you be so kind to give me some advice?
> > I think the 'AB.tumor' column may help me, but I cannot understand the meaning of this column. It seems that the sum of each row of the AB.tumor does not equal 1, but equals 1 - Bf.
> > Thanks!
> >
> > Yang
> >
> > 在 2017年3月23日星期四 UTC+8下午5:52:35，Francesco Favero写道：
> > > Hi, the size of the pileup is of the compressed or uncompressed file?
> > > Unless you are splitting the process in multiple chromosomes you will not take full advantage of the 20 CPUs of your machine. If you have indexed pileup (or the original bams) you could try the new sequenza-utils library, in development.
> > > Otherwise, to speed up the script provided in the package (around 6x) you can use the pypy interpreter instead of the standard python2.7.
> > >
> > > The size of the final file should be roughly the same as your pileup, but it might be considerable less if you have a very high coverage WES. In order to process the file it in R, there is an additional binning step you should perform. for WES I usually use 50nt binning (for WGS 200nt). In my experience the binned file should be less then 1Gb and usually around 300Mb
> > >
> > > Francesco
> > >
> > > > On 22 Mar 2017, at 17.39, 11033...@qq.com wrote:
> > > >
> > > > HI, I'm using sequenza to analyze my WES data. The size of my pileup file is about 25G per sample. I run the sequenza-utils pileup2seqz with 20 CPUs and now 3 hour has passed. It has not finished its work with one sample.
> > > > It is said in the 2015 paper that a sample can be finished within 4 hours with 1 CPU. Why it is so slow on my sample?
